title: Let CTP insurers compete on price, with premiums that reflect risk
action: Allow compulsory third-party insurers to compete on price within regulated bands, with premiums that better reflect each vehicle's and driver's risk, as South Australia did when it opened CTP to private insurers.
why: Premiums that ignore risk mean safer drivers subsidise riskier ones, and fixed prices remove the incentive for insurers to compete on cost and service.

evidence.source: Australia's Future Tax System: Report to the Treasurer, Part One (Henry review)
evidence.quote: States should improve compulsory third party insurance to better reflect individual risks.

precedents.what: Opened CTP insurance to private insurers competing on price in 2019.
